title: Cones of Theta Graphs are Enumeratively Chromatic-Choosable
summary: Chromatic choosability is a fundamental notion in list coloring. A graph $G$ is chromatic-choosable if its chromatic number $χ(G)$ equals its list chromatic number $χ_{\ell}(G)$. In 1990, Kostochka and Sidorenko introduced the list color function of a graph $G$, denoted by $P_{\ell}(G,m)$, which is the list-coloring analogue of its chromatic polynomial $P(G,m)$. A graph $G$ is enumeratively chromatic-choosable if $P_{\ell}(G,m)=P(G,m)$ for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$.
